OUTSIDE_THE_STUDY: All runs below used Qiskit 2.3.0 and 2.3.1, which are not P, B or F of any Phase D event, plus synthetic test files. No study version was timed, collected or run by the runner. Data root /tmp/phase_d_dry (not phase_d/data).

prepare.note: wheel download + sha256 check, venv + pinned install, sdist download + sha256 check, test/ extraction

small_modules.wall_per_file_s: 1.00-1.20 (process start, qiskit import, collection, 0.2 s poll granularity)

robustness_checks.per_test_timeout: synthetic test sleeping 1000 s killed after 60 s, recorded outcome 'timeout' duration 60.0, file relaunched with completed+timed-out tests deselected (3 launches incl. crash)
robustness_checks.crash: synthetic os.abort() recorded outcome 'crash' (rc -6), file relaunched, remaining test recorded
robustness_checks.external_kill_resume: tool call killed at 120 s during a 6 x 20 s file (2 tests recorded, test 3 in progress lost); next call resumed with the 2 completed tests deselected and finished the remaining 4 (82.8 s)
robustness_checks.hard_limit_kill: not separately triggered (same kill path as the timeout; the external kill exercised the worse case)
robustness_checks.multi_path_unit: after the runner change that runs a backported file in the same process as its logical file: a two-file unit (test_1q.py + test_apply_layout.py) on 2.3.1 recorded 20 tests in one process (2.9 s)

backport_mechanics_on_2.3.1.note: all 8 frozen backport modules run against 2.3.1's own test tree (2.3.1 contains every fix except D4's and D5's features); checks importability and the inherited-test hiding only
backport_mechanics_on_2.3.1.D4: 3 failed (exact-circuit assertion needs a 2.5 feature, as on 2.4.2)

fixes_made_because_of_the_dry_run: node-id normalization: ddt names embed '..._object_at_0x772b46dca620_...' (underscores), so the address pattern was changed from ' at 0x...' to any '0x' + >= 6 hex digits
calibration workload enlarged 5x (0.05 s -> 0.25 s per repetition) to reduce noise
backported test files now run in the same pytest process right after their logical file (warm process, as if appended), instead of as a separate cold process
analysis_pipeline: phase_d_analysis.py ran end to end on the dry-run data with phase_d/dryrun/dryrun_ledger.json (event DRY: P 2.3.0, B 2.3.1, no F-check, no backport) -> dryrun_analysis_output.json; suite 62 tests, est/real suite cost 60.49/60.48 s (dominated by the synthetic 60-s timeout), k measured 1.002

runtime_model_for_collection.per_pass_seconds: about 1.0 s per file of runner overhead (106-115 files) + test time; test time from the 2026-10-18 slice runs of 2.2.2/2.2.3 (pytest-reported 97-101 s for the whole slice, file-level only) -> about 200 s per pass for 2.0-2.2; 2.4.2/2.5.x collect about 2.9x more tests (7686 for 2.5.2) -> about 300-400 s per pass (not timed)

synthetic_test_files: phase_d/dryrun/synthetic_tests/dryrun_synthetic_*.py (renamed from test_synthetic_*.py, the names in the dry-run data, so that pytest never collects them by accident)
